subject: Assured uptime bundling and escalation roles
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@stratoscloud.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA questions — uptime targets + oncall coverage

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Two follow-ups from our side as procurement and engineering prep for the SOW:1) We need an explicit pricing line for an "Assured" uptime tier (99.99% availability) versus Standard (99.9%). Please include per-month committed capacity and the per-hour oncall retainer cost.2) How do escalation roles map — who at Redwood is the first point of contact vs the engineering escalation path? We have a separate team that will need guaranteed response windows and a named escalation owner for P1s.

Also, procurement asked if you offer a volume-based uplift discount at 2x committed capacity.

Can you send a concise price table and an escalation matrix we can insert into our contract review?

Best,
Elaine
Director of Platform Engineering
Stratos Cloud

---

On Tue, 1 Jun 2027 at 11:05 AM Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com> wrote:
To: Elaine Park <elaine@stratoscloud.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA questions — uptime targets + oncall coverage

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a short price table and a draft escalation matrix for review (SLA_Prices_v3.pdf). Summary below:  

- Assured (99.99%): base monthly fee = $55,000; includes dedicated capacity reservation for up to 1.5x committed throughput. P1 response (acknowledge) within 15 minutes, engineered triage within 1 hour. Oncall retainer = $1,250/hr after the first 4 hours per incident.
- Standard (99.9%): base monthly fee = $22,500; shared capacity; P1 acknowledge within 30 minutes, triage within 4 hours. Oncall retainer = $900/hr after first 8 hours.
- Volume uplift pricing: 15% discount on base fee at 2x committed capacity; larger discounts are tied to multi-quarter commit.

Escalation matrix (high level):  
- Tier 1: Customer Success manager (CSM) — initial intake and SLA verification (names to be finalized).
- Tier 2: Production Support Engineer (Redwood Support) — 24/7 triage for P1s.
- Tier 3: On-call SRE + Engineering on rotation (named escalation owner assigned per region).
- Exec escalation: Vivek Kulkarni (cc'd) for contract-level exceptions and credit adjudication.

I've looped in Ben (finance) and Vivek to confirm the discount envelope and retainer structure. Please confirm timing for a short call if you want to walk the numbers.

Attachments: SLA_Prices_v3.pdf (price table, escalation matrix), redwood-dpa-supplement.docx (data processing addendum)

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

On Thu, 3 Jun 2027 at 08:47 AM Elaine Park <elaine@stratoscloud.com> wrote:
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stratoscloud.com
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA questions — uptime targets + oncall coverage

Priya —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from procurement and our cloud ops lead:  

- The oncall retainer wording needs to be clearer on the "first X hours included" vs invoiced hours. Procurement prefers a flat monthly retainer cap for predictable billing (e.g., $20k/mo) rather than open-ended hourly.
- For escalation owners, we need a named person at Tier 3 for contract signature (we can't accept roles only). Can Redwood provide a primary contact and two alternates for the first year?
- Regarding credits: how are uptime credits calculated if a partial outage affects only one region? We need regionalized credit logic in the SOW.

We can be flexible on price if we get predictability on billing and named escalation owners. Would your team accept a capped monthly oncall retainer and a templated regional credit schedule?

Elaine

---

On Mon, 7 Jun 2027 at 15:28:00 -0700 Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com> wrote:
To: Elaine Park <elaine@stratoscloud.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, procurement@stratoscloud.com
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA questions — uptime targets + oncall coverage

Elaine — appreciate the specifics, this is helpful. Proposal update below and next steps.  

1) Capped monthly oncall retainer: Redwood can offer a $20,000/month capped retainer that covers up to 40 hours of oncall engineering time for incident remediation. Hours beyond the cap billed at $950/hr. This replaces the per-hour retainer line in the prior doc.
2) Named escalation owners: we can provide a primary Tier 3 escalation owner and two alternates for the first 12 months. Proposed primary: Jordan Blake (Lead SRE, Americas) — contact jordan_blake@redwood.com — mobile included in appendix. Alternates: Marcus Lin (SRE) and Olga Petrov (Senior Engineer). We'll include full contact info in the SOW.
3) Regionalized uptime credits: credits will be prorated by affected region traffic percentage. Proposed table in the attached revised SLA_Prices_v3.pdf shows specific credit slabs (e.g., 99.99->credit X, 99.9->credit Y) and a formula for partial-region impact.

Discounting: Given the predictability ask and 2x capacity uplift, we can move to a 20% discount on the Assured base fee for a 12-month committed contract and a two-quarter prepay. Ben, if that's acceptable to finance, we'll flag for the commercial term sheet.

Next steps:  
- I'll attach the revised SLA and the appendix with named escalation contacts and a capped oncall amendment.
- If acceptable, I'll push the commercial term sheet and DocuSign link (see draft link) so procurement can review.

Ben: please confirm whether finance is OK with the 20% uplift discount and the proposed prepay cadence. Vivek: any exec comments on escalation/credit language?

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-minute call tomorrow to finalize if that helps.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
